EasyBCD won't always work, or not at all, in that case the ability to add Non-Microsoft OS Boot options to the WIndows Boot Manager won't be possible, so far I've tested this and found it to be an issue on VMWare Workstation's implementation of the EFI and my ASUS Laptop's UEFI, this is the error. The only way to boot into both Windows and Linux is using the GRUB2 bootloader that is installed after installing Linux.

If you ever want to restore the Windows Boot Manager as your default bootloader, this will have to be done by rearranging the boot order in the UEFI setup and set "Windows Boot Manager" above the entry already above it which for a lot of you will probably be "mint", it's fairly painless since every operating system installed for UEFI keeps it's boot files in a hidden FAT32 partition that all installed OSes share for .efi boot file storage, so switching between the GRUB2 and Windows Boot Manager is fairly non-intrusive.
